There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

Recent findings suggest that this particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

Sources indicate that so to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

Sources indicate that “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba noted. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a substantial career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Recent findings suggest that floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

In a recent development, chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Sources indicate that allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was notable for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca remarked.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

In a recent development, well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

Industry observers note that big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

Sources indicate that his shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Industry observers note that what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Sources indicate that norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

Industry observers note that and the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

According to recent reports, keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

Sources indicate that his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

Industry observers note that these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

In a recent development, philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

Gli accertamenti a Rozzano hanno rilevato un problema ai flessori della coscia destra; non sono indicati i tempi di recupero.

Hakan Calhanoglu ha riportato un risentimento muscolare ai flessori della coscia destra. È l’esito degli esami svolti in mattinata dal centrocampista dell’Inter dopo lo stop contro l’Atalanta. I nerazzurri proveranno a recuperarlo per la Supercoppa del 22 dicembre contro la Lazio. La notizia è riportata da Gianlucadimarzio.

Recent findings suggest that il centrocampista si è sottoposto agli accertamenti strumentali presso l’Istituto Clinico Humanitas di Rozzano. Nel comunicato, l’Inter precisa: «Hakan Çalhanoğlu si è sottoposto questa mattina a esami strumentali presso l'Istituto Clinico Humanitas di Rozzano. Gli esami hanno evidenziato un risentimento muscolare ai flessori della coscia destra».

Calhanoglu era uscito nel primo tempo della partita contro l’Atalanta per un problema alla coscia destra. Come riportato da Sky Sport, il 24 novembre non si è allenato con il resto della squadra alla vigilia della gara con lo Stoccarda: stava svolgendo gli esami strumentali.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.
  • In a recent development, there were, however, some noticeable improvements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

In a recent development, there were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent strategy for creating chances.

But the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a new manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace.

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel complications in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

In a recent development, new boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

Sources indicate that ‘That was the major positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’.

Defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

Sources indicate that coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how rapidly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat.

According to recent reports, anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

That is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant issue.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition swiftly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni.

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that the Coventry boss said: ‘It’s a big win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s notable to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

It has been revealed that ‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that il turno infrasettimanale di Serie B fa rima con gol. Sono state infatti ben 24 le marcature nelle prime sei gare del tredicesimo turno che si gioca su due giorni con Benevento, Cesena e Palermo a siglare delle vere e proprie goleade: 5-0 per i sanniti contro un Empoli in caduta libera, 5-1 per i romagnoli contro un Ascoli che fin qui si era dimostrato fra le più quadrate del torneo, e 4-1 per i siciliani contro un SudTirol che continua a essere troppo altalenante. A questi si aggiungono i quattro gol di Castellammare di Stabia, dove il Catanzaro conquista la seconda vittoria con un altro 3-1, mentre quasi passano in secondo piano i successi di misura della Virtus Entella (2-1 sul Verona in rimonta) e della Carrarese sul campo del Vicenza (1-0 il finale). Ora toccherà alle altre otto che scenderanno in campo domani tenere alta la bandiera dello spettacolo.

Tanti gol, tanti protagonisti, ma due in particolare si sono presi la scena: il primo è Cristian Shpendi del Cesena che con una tripletta, la prima in Serie B, eguaglia i 12 gol messi a segno lo scorso anno (in 37 gare) viaggiando a una media di quasi una rete a partita e candidandosi a uomo mercato per gennaio; il secondo è invece Dennis Johnsen a cui il ritorno nel ruolo di esterno d’attacco ha solo che fatto bene. Una doppietta e un assist che ritoccano ulteriormente un rendimento sopra la media: nove reti e sei passaggi decisivi in 13 presenze per il norvegese che sta già facendo meglio dell’anno che lo consacrò come protagonista assoluto a Cremona dove conquistò anche la promozione.

Juve Stabia – Catanzaro 1-3 28’ Antonini (C), 45’+4’ Pecorino (C), 53’ Ruggero (C), 72’ Maistro (J) Benevento – Empoli 5-0 5’ Okereke, 30’ Prisco, 46’ Tumminello, 74’ Siatounis, 78’ Cherubini Cesena – Ascoli 5-1 33’ Caprini (C), 47’ Gelli (C), 68, 83’ e 87’ Shpendi (C), 86’ Corradini (A) Vicenza – Carrarese 0-1 7’ Schiavi Palermo – SudTirol 4-1 7’ e 68’ Johnsen (P), 14’ Pohjanpalo (P), 45’ Vavassori (P), 52’ Rispoli (S) Virtus Entella - Hellas Verona 2-1 18’ Sarr (HV), 33’ Corona (VE), 65’ Cuppone (VE).

Alla vigilia della gara contro i nerazzurri, il sito ufficiale del club tedesco elogia il Settore Giovanile dell'Inter.

Sources indicate that "Se si chiede agli esperti di calcio italiani quale sia il miglior settore giovanile del Paese, i nomi che vengono citati più frequentemente sono quelli dell’Atalanta e della Roma. Ma anche l’Inter può dire la sua in questa discussione, pur non rientrando nella ristretta cerchia delle prime due. A parlare per il club nerazzurro non è soltanto la lista dei giocatori cresciuti in casa, tra cui figurano leggende come Giuseppe Meazza, Walter Zenga, Leonardo Bonucci e Mario Balotelli, ma anche i risultati ottenuti dalle formazioni giovanili. L’Inter è infatti il club che ha vinto più volte il campionato Primavera. Nell'attuale rosa della prima squadra, quattro prodotti del vivaio hanno già trovato spazio in questa stagione: Federico Dimarco, Aleksandar Stankovic, Pio Esposito e Matteo Lavelli".

Sources indicate that "La formazione dell'Inter impegnata in Youth League è composta in larga parte da elementi della Primavera. Uno dei profili più interessanti, tuttavia, milita già nell'Under 23, impegnata nel campionato di Serie C: si tratta del difensore centrale croato Leon Jakirovic, 18 anni, considerato uno dei maggiori talenti della sua generazione nel ruolo e già vicino alla prima squadra. Il suo abituale compagno di reparto nell'Under 23 e in Youth League, Andrea Donato, non sarà invece a disposizione mercoledì, così come il portiere Carlo Galliera. Entrambi saranno assenti a causa della partecipazione al Mondiale Under 17 con la nazionale italiana".

Fiorentina e Milan pagano 5mila euro ciascuna; provvedimenti anche per Atalanta, Genoa, Monza, Udinese e Bologna.

According to recent reports, il Giudice sportivo ha inflitto 10.000 euro di ammenda alla Roma per oggetti lanciati dai suoi sostenitori durante la gara e 8.000 euro al Como per il ritardo di circa quattro minuti nell’inizio del secondo tempo. Secondo quanto riportato da Giudice sportivo, Sanzionate anche Fiorentina, Milan, Atalanta, Genoa, Monza, Udinese e Bologna.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that alla Roma sono contestati il lancio di tre petardi e di un accendino sul terreno di gioco, oltre a un fumogeno e una bottiglietta di plastica nel recinto di gioco. L’ammenda da 10.000 euro è stata attenuata ai sensi dell’articolo 29, comma 1, lettera b) del CGS.

Per l’Atalanta la sanzione è di 4.000 euro. I suoi sostenitori hanno lanciato un accendino sul terreno di gioco e due bottigliette nel recinto di gioco. Anche in questo caso l’ammenda è stata attenuata in base all’articolo 29, comma 1, lettera b) del CGS.

It has been revealed that il Como è stato multato di 8.000 euro a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva per aver provocato ingiustificatamente un ritardo di circa quattro minuti nell’inizio del secondo tempo. Il provvedimento segnala la recidiva reiterata.

Sources indicate that ammende di 5.000 euro ciascuna per Fiorentina e Milan, sempre a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva. La Fiorentina ha causato ingiustificatamente un ritardo di circa due minuti nell’inizio del secondo tempo; il Milan, nella stessa fase della gara, un ritardo di circa tre minuti. Per entrambe è indicata la recidiva.

Industry observers note that il Genoa deve pagare 3.000 euro per aver provocato ingiustificatamente, a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva, un ritardo di circa due minuti nell’inizio del primo tempo. Stessa cifra per il Monza, al quale è contestato un ritardo ingiustificato di circa due minuti nell’inizio della ripresa, sempre a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva.

Il TAS ribalta tutto: la Coppa d'Africa torna al Senegal, ma il Marocco annuncia battaglia

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that la Coppa d'Africa 2025 si è conclusa con una vicenda destinata a lasciare il segno nella storia del calcio africano.
  • Recent findings suggest that tutto era cominciato il 18 gennaio, durante la finale tra Senegal e Marocco.
  • Il Marocco aveva contestato l'esito della finale, sostenendo che l'uscita temporanea dal campo dei giocatori avversari dovesse essere considerata un abbandono della partita e comportare quindi una sconfitta a tavolino.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that la Coppa d'Africa 2025 si è conclusa con una vicenda destinata a lasciare il segno nella storia del calcio africano. A distanza di oltre dieci mesi dalla finale disputata a Rabat, il Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport ha accolto il ricorso del Senegal, riconoscendo nuovamente alla nazionale il titolo conquistato sul campo. Una decisione che ha ribaltato quanto stabilito a marzo dalla Confederazione Africana di Calcio, che aveva invece assegnato la vittoria al Marocco per 3-0 a tavolino. Il verdetto del TAS ha riaperto una questione che sembrava ormai indirizzata, ma la reazione della federazione marocchina lascia intendere che la vicenda potrebbe non essere ancora arrivata al suo ultimo capitolo.

Recent findings suggest that tutto era cominciato il 18 gennaio, durante la finale tra Senegal e Marocco. Nei minuti conclusivi della partita, dopo un calcio di rigore assegnato ai padroni di casa, la panchina senegalese aveva protestato in maniera plateale, arrivando a richiamare i giocatori negli spogliatoi. A evitare che la situazione degenerasse ulteriormente era stato Sadio Mané, rimasto in campo per convincere i compagni a tornare sul terreno di gioco. Una volta ripresa la partita, Brahim Diaz aveva fallito il penalty tentando un cucchiaio, mentre nei tempi supplementari Pape Gueye aveva firmato la rete decisiva per l'1-0 del Senegal.

Il Marocco aveva contestato l'esito della finale, sostenendo che l'uscita temporanea dal campo dei giocatori avversari dovesse essere considerata un abbandono della partita e comportare quindi una sconfitta a tavolino. La questione era così finita davanti agli organi di giustizia sportiva.

Sources indicate that il 17 marzo 2026 la Commissione d'Appello della CAF aveva accolto il ricorso della federazione marocchina, ribaltando il risultato della finale e assegnando al Marocco la vittoria per 3-0 a tavolino. Una decisione che aveva privato il Senegal del titolo conquistato sul campo e spinto la federazione a rivolgersi al Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport per ottenere giustizia.

Sources indicate that la battaglia legale si è conclusa, almeno per quanto riguarda il procedimento davanti al TAS, martedì 24 novembre 2026. Il tribunale di Losanna ha infatti accolto il ricorso senegalese, annullando la decisione della Commissione d'Appello della CAF e ripristinando integralmente il risultato della finale del 18 gennaio: 1-0 dopo i tempi supplementari. Il Senegal è così tornato ufficialmente in possesso della Coppa d'Africa 2025.

In a recent development, la Federazione Senegalese di Calcio ha accolto con "profonda soddisfazione" il verdetto, diffondendo un comunicato nel quale ha confermato di aver ricevuto la notifica ufficiale della sentenza. La FSF ha sottolineato che il TAS ha annullato la decisione della CAF del 17 marzo e ripristinato il risultato maturato sul campo.

Sources indicate that nel comunicato, la federazione ha definito la decisione una vittoria dell'equità sportiva, ribadendo che "la verità di una partita si stabilisce esclusivamente sul campo, sotto la tutela del diritto sportivo". La FSF ha inoltre ringraziato i giocatori, lo staff tecnico, i propri legali, il presidente della Repubblica, il governo senegalese e tutti i tifosi che hanno sostenuto la nazionale durante la vicenda.

Il presidente Abdoulaye Fall ha commentato così il verdetto: "Il Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport ha reso giustizia allo sport". Il numero uno della federazione ha poi voluto sottolineare i rapporti con il Paese avversario, ribadendo i "legami di fratellanza" che uniscono il Senegal al Marocco e alla sua federazione. Un messaggio di distensione, accompagnato dalla volontà di guardare al futuro con fiducia ed entusiasmo.

According to recent reports, di segno opposto la reazione della Federazione Reale Marocchina di Calcio, che ha preso atto della decisione del TAS senza nascondere la propria insoddisfazione. Nel comunicato ufficiale, la FRMF ha contestato il fatto che le proprie richieste non siano state prese in considerazione, facendo riferimento a presunte irregolarità che, secondo la federazione, avrebbero compromesso il procedimento e messo in discussione l'integrità e la credibilità della decisione.

Recent findings suggest that in particolare, la federazione marocchina ha sostenuto che sarebbe stato confermato un contatto tra l'arbitro tedesco Ulrich Haas e il presidente della federazione senegalese Abdoulaye Fall, avvenuto 48 ore prima della pronuncia. Si tratta di una contestazione contenuta nella posizione ufficiale del Marocco, che non viene presentata come un accertamento del TAS.

La FRMF ha inoltre criticato la decisione per non aver tenuto conto, a suo giudizio, delle indicazioni più recenti di IFAB e FIFA riguardo ai giocatori che abbandonano il terreno di gioco senza l'autorizzazione dell'arbitro e alle relative conseguenze disciplinari.

La federazione ha infine annunciato l'intenzione di avviare "tutte le procedure legali necessarie per contestare la decisione del TAS". Il verdetto restituisce dunque il titolo al Senegal, ma il Marocco non sembra intenzionato ad accettarlo senza ulteriori iniziative.

A commentare la vicenda ai microfoni di TMW è stato anche Malu Mpasinkatu, dirigente sportivo ed esperto di calcio africano. La sua posizione sul verdetto è netta: "La decisione è giusta in quanto rispecchia il verdetto del campo. Il Senegal aveva vinto la finale contro il Marocco e merita questo successo".

Mpasinkatu ha però espresso dispiacere per il modo in cui verrà ricordata quella partita e, più in generale, un'edizione della Coppa d'Africa che aveva offerto tanti spunti positivi: "A me dispiace solo che quella finale, una partita bellissima di un torneo altrettanto bello, venga ricordata soltanto per quell'episodio e non per tutto ciò che di bello ha mostrato".

Infine, Mpasinkatu ha voluto allargare lo sguardo ai rapporti tra i due Paesi, invitando a non confondere la controversia sportiva con i legami tra le rispettive popolazioni: "Marocco e Senegal sono due Paesi molto amici, i due popoli si vogliono bene". La Coppa d'Africa, ha ricordato, rappresenta un momento di festa per tutto il continente e il calcio ha la capacità di unire i popoli. Proprio per questo, ha concluso, è un peccato che un'edizione così bella venga ricordata soprattutto per l'episodio finale e per tutto ciò che ne è seguito.

Wouter Vrancken stated Hearts’ ruthless 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kabore both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal taking the tally to eight without reply.

And Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

The 47-year-old remarked: 'The best performance? Of course.

'When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence.

'You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

Stuart Findlay heads in the eighth to cap a remarkable evening for Hearts at Dens Park.

'When it’s 0-0 and 1-0, you don’t feel as confident so maybe you don’t have the bravery to do it or show it.

Industry observers note that 'It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet.

'I was very happy with the performance, not only the score.

'We had the talks before our days off, they were really honest and open. It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch.

'You can talk as much as you want but if you can’t show it on the pitch it doesn’t mean anything.

'When you do it like this it’s the first step.

'But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

“The message to the players is feet back on the ground because after the last break we started with a 5-0 win over St Mirren then had difficult moments.

'It was ruthless in the game today but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight.'.

Claudio Braga fires home a fifth goal for Vrancken's side in the demolition job.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and performance.

He noted: 'It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

'I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that.

'We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and reveals grit.

'We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

'We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight.

'Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility.

'All areas of our performance was disappointing.

'I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

Sources indicate that tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel stated. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

Sources indicate that “This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He remarked: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

Industry observers note that “It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

It has been revealed that “If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel remarked. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel noted. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

Recent findings suggest that “So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I noted, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”.

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always remarked he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”.

In a recent development, tuchel stated that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

According to recent reports, “I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

Sources indicate that “It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”.

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”.

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”.

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has mentioned to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel notes that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to says he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”.

Tuchel notes he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”.

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

Industry observers note that “When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”.

Sources indicate that tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel claims the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”.

Industry observers note that tuchel claims his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s vital to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has said the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

Sources indicate that no questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

Recent findings suggest that ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”.

According to recent reports, “They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a fresh competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”.

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

It has been revealed that 5 - Alex Scott is the only midfielder in the Premier League this season to rank in the top five for times he has won possession (3rd), for the number of duels contested (=4th) and for total distance covered (5th).Sprightly. pic.twitter.com/xfVzme7JXj.

Recent findings suggest that jason Steele’s inclusion is effectively a call-up. He was at the World Cup as a “fourth” goalkeeper for training – and going to country and western gigs in Kansas – but was not part of the official 26-man squad.

The significant ‘loser’ from the World Cup squad in being left out by Thomas Tuchel is Arsenal’s Noni Madueke. It is understood the place of his club team-mate Eberechi Eze was also in question, but the 28-year-old has been included, partly because of the unavailability of other players. Hopefully Thomas Tuchel will explain all later.

The absence of Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White is puzzling.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the top-scoring Englishman in the Premier League since the start of last season.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN STICKS IT IN!" pic.twitter.com/UJ54wPGytV.

Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the first games of the 2026-27 season, as the Three Lions begin a upcoming Uefa Nations League campaign.

The head coach has selected a 27-man squad for the four-game window, which takes place between September 21 and October 6.

There’s a return to the Three Lions squad for a number of players following the start of the upcoming campaign with their clubs, with the likes of Cole Palmer, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Lewis Hall, Rio Ngumoha, Jarrad Branthwaite, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott all selected.

And there’s a place in the squad for Trent Alexander-Arnold, alongside his Real Madrid teammate Jude Bellingham.

Industry observers note that here it is! 🤩Thomas Tuchel's first #ThreeLions squad of the 2026-27 season 🦁 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿.

Ivan Toney likely to miss out as he is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24.

Nine weeks have passed since the agonising semi-final collapse to Argentina and Tuchel can expect a grilling about his reflections.

He will need to rebuild trust with supporters heading into a cycle that culminates with a home Euros in 2028.

Eberechi Eze could be left out of the England squad confirmed this morning by Thomas Tuchel ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. The Arsenal midfielder has made six appearances for his club so far this season but has only started two of those games and none in the Premier League.

The 28-year-old played four times for England during the last World Cup but Tuchel is expected to shake up his forward options. There is an expectation that there will be a recall for Chelsea’s Cole Palmer.

Breaking: MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.
  • It has been revealed that and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

It has been revealed that and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

Recent findings suggest that it looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

Messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

Sources indicate that that’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers.

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top.

Sources indicate that however, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

It has been revealed that just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up substantial-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

Jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

It was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Industry observers note that djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park.

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

According to recent reports, the South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

Sources indicate that an initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

In a recent development, motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Remarked, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side.

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Industry observers note that naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

Industry observers note that it shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

According to recent reports, non è stata una passeggiata di salute. Sotto la pioggia copiosa del Sinigaglia, il Como ha conquistato la sua quarta vittoria della Champions League ed è a un passo dall'aritmetica qualificazione tra le prime 24 forze d'Europa. Un rigore sbagliato da Da Cunha, il doppio salvataggio di Robert Sanchez al termine del primo tempo, mentre il gioiello di Luis Milla all'incrocio dei pali ha deciso l'incontro 1-0. Il Como vince e vede la qualificazione ai playoff.

Sources indicate that "Per il Como non è normale fare 8 vittorie su 9", ha esordito l'allenatore del Como, Cesc Fabregas in conferenza stampa post-partita. Soffermandosi ad ampio spettro sui risultati ottenuti finora lungo il cammino del club lariano da quando il catalano ha in mano le redini della squadra: "Sappiamo che è un progetto speciale. Sono il primo che celebra 5 minuti e poi andiamo alla prossima. Ma se torniamo a tre anni fa, è vero, siamo cresciuti velocemente. Dobbiamo godercela almeno un attimo. Viviamo in un mondo che se perdi con il Frosinone ti ammazzano. Bisogna capire quello che sta succedendo, con umiltà e la voglia di lavorare. Si sta facendo una cosa diversa e speciale. All'esterno sembra una normalità. Quando sono arrivato quattro anni e mezzo fa, io ad allenare tre anni fa. Lo valorizziamo, piano piano, per ritrovare le forze. Voi scriverete che siamo meglio della Juventus, ma è la squadra più storica d'Italia. Noi dobbiamo trovare la forza per fare la partita perfetta un'altra volta".

Industry observers note that marko Nikolic, tecnico dell'AEK Atene, "Per me è una delle squadre più forti in Europa. Complimenti al suo allenatore, sapevamo fosse difficile giocare con il Como. Ha fatto 4 gol con il Manchester United e capite che è difficile giocare contro una squadra così. Hanno uno straordinario arsenale offensivo, ma sono contento per come abbiamo affrontato la partita. Avremmo potuto perderla però in altri modi, non con questo errore. Pazienza. Comunque era una squadra molto giovane e interessante".

Enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni a Sky Sport, dopo il pari con il Napoli in Champions League: “Il problema difensivo è chiaro e dobbiamo risolverlo. Per il resto sono sereno, contro un blocco basso come quello del Napoli è difficile attaccarlo, stiamo concedendo troppi gol e dobbiamo lavorare. Non è facile, dopo dieci anni con lo stesso allenatore, è difficile per tutti, per noi, per l’Arsenal. Ci vuole un pò di tempo, ma in generale sono contento, a parte qualche lacuna, abbiamo fatto bene, ma alla prima occasione concediamo gol. Noi ci aspettavamo il Napoli come l’ho visto con Torino e Lazio, ho pensato di portare il cerchio aperto dove c’era spazio, ma non siamo riusciti a creare. Era questo il pensiero, il regista lo può fare Bouaddi, tre dietro e attaccare con sei giocatori, lo può fare anche Anderson, ma cercavo anche equilibrio con palla e senza palla, sto cercando di mantenere le cose semplici come fatto in passato, dobbiamo trovare il giusto equilibrio tra le due fasi”.

Sources indicate that overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

Recent findings suggest that in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Recent findings suggest that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

It has been revealed that not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

According to recent reports, it was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

According to recent reports, both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Recent findings suggest that another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

Recent findings suggest that this was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Sources indicate that arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

It has been revealed that “There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta noted. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

Sources indicate that “It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta noted. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always vital to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

Industry observers note that two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

What a start for Newcastle United and what will really please manager Matthias Jaissle is the way both goals have come from his players winning important tackles.

It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the upcoming buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever upcoming terminology to describe an old idea.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

According to recent reports, brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

It has been revealed that that 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

It has been revealed that with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Sources indicate that elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that dopo la trasferta contro l'Atalanta, l'Inter ritrova San Siro.
  • "I ragazzi di Hoeness, figlio di Dieter e nipote di Uli, in Champions hanno collezionato sette punti.
  • It has been revealed that "Ermedin Demirovic è la punta dello Stoccarda.

Recent findings suggest that dopo la trasferta contro l'Atalanta, l'Inter ritrova San Siro. I nerazzurri domani scenderanno in campo dove affronteranno lo Stoccarda nella gara valida per la quinta giornata della Fase Campionato della UEFA Champions League. La Gazzetta dello Sport analizza la squadra tedesca, in particolare i punti di forza.

"I ragazzi di Hoeness, figlio di Dieter e nipote di Uli, in Champions hanno collezionato sette punti. In campionato sono a 13. Nell'ultimo turno hanno pareggiato 0-0 con lo Schalke 04. Squadra ostica, difficile da leggere, capace di segnare 27 gol in 16 partite. Football Meets Data aveva sentenziato il "miglior calendario di tutta la Champions" a inizio competizione. Fin qui hanno battuto Viking e Slovan Bratislava, pareggiato 1-1 con l'Atletico e perso con il Galatasaray".

It has been revealed that "Ermedin Demirovic è la punta dello Stoccarda. Quest'anno ha segnato 9 gol in 16 partite, di cui quattro nella grande coppa in altrettante gare. Dal 2024 a oggi ha segnato 41 gol in 103 partite con lo Stoccarda. Nel 2025 ha vinto la Coppa di Germania. La storia di Deniz Undav è il manifesto del sacrificio. A 17 anni fu scartato dal Werder Brema perché era "troppo basso" - parole di un vecchio scout -, così inizia a lavorare in fabbrica per duecento euro al mese. Prima di emergere al St. Gilloise, in Belgio, s'è fatto largo nelle serie minori tedesche. Grazie ai gol con lo Stoccarda - 59 in 4 anni - è arrivato anche in nazionale. Media invidiabile: 9 reti in 13 partite".

"Lo Stoccarda ha dei giocatori niente male. Il primo: zoom su Jamie Leweling, 25 anni, esterno offensivo nato a Norimberga. La stagione scorsa ha centrato 11 gol e altrettanti assist: non male. Un altro da tenere d'occhio è Maximilian Mittelstadt, terzino sinistro offensivo. Quest'anno ha segnato due gol e servito un assist. Fari anche su Bilal El Khannouss, fantasista marocchino riscattato in estate per circa 20 milioni. Due gol a referto. Chiudiamo con un difensore di vent'anni. Il titolare della retroguardia è Finn Jeltsch, 2006, partito dal 1' in Bundesliga in sette occasioni su dieci".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

Il Napoli torna da Manchester con un punto, qualche rimpianto e soprattutto tante certezze in più. La squadra di Massimiliano Allegri pareggia per 2-2 all'Etihad Stadium contro il Manchester City, al termine di una prova collettiva di grande spessore. Gli azzurri soffrono senza mai disunirsi, limitano le occasioni degli inglesi e sfiorano il vantaggio già nel primo tempo con Beukema, fermato da un ottimo Donnarumma. Nella ripresa Hojlund sblocca il risultato con un diagonale preciso su assist di Gilmour, prima del pareggio firmato da Bouaddi. Nel momento di maggiore difficoltà, Noa Lang riporta avanti il Napoli con uno splendido destro al volo su cross di Spinazzola, ma una prodezza individuale di Cherki all'86' fissa il risultato sul definitivo 2-2. Gli azzurri salgono a quattro punti dopo cinque giornate di Champions League, mentre i Citizens raggiungono quota dieci. Al di là delle implicazioni in termini di classifica, la notizia migliore per Allegri è la risposta della squadra, arrivata peraltro in piena emergenza.

According to recent reports, nel post-partita, ai microfoni di Sky Sport, Allegri ha sottolineato i progressi della squadra, soprattutto nella gestione delle due fasi: “I ragazzi sono stati bravi nell'uscita palla, tecnicamente abbiamo fatto buone cose e soprattutto bene nel non possesso nel rallentare l'azione del City. Ci deve essere l'amaro in bocca per la mancata vittoria anche se il pareggio è il risultato più giusto”. Il tecnico si è assunto anche parte delle responsabilità per le precedenti difficoltà difensive, evidenziando il cambio di atteggiamento visto a Manchester: “Stasera loro per far gol hanno dovuto sudare e questo è l'atteggiamento giusto per vincere le partite”. Tra i temi più importanti della serata, però, c'è anche il futuro di Kevin De Bruyne. Il belga ha ricevuto una standing ovation dal pubblico dell'Etihad al momento della sostituzione, prima di abbracciare Allegri a bordocampo. L'allenatore ha poi allontanato le voci di un possibile addio a gennaio, esprimendo fiducia sulla permanenza del centrocampista: “Ne parlerà con la società. Kevin è un ragazzo serio e credo che rimarrà fino a giugno”. Una presa di posizione che fa seguito alle dichiarazioni del direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna, che nel prepartita aveva ricordato come il belga fosse sotto contratto fino al termine della stagione, con un'opzione per il rinnovo.

Di tutt'altro tenore l'analisi di Enzo Maresca, che ha riconosciuto le difficoltà difensive della propria squadra e i meriti dell'organizzazione tattica del Napoli: “Il problema difensivo è abbastanza chiaro e dobbiamo risolverlo. Per il resto sono abbastanza sereno, sempre difficile attaccare un blocco basso come quello del Napoli”. L'allenatore italiano ha spiegato anche le ragioni delle proprie scelte iniziali, riconoscendo come l'ingresso degli esterni offensivi abbia permesso ai Citizens di creare maggiori pericoli. Maresca ha poi invitato ad avere pazienza per il nuovo corso del Manchester City dopo un decennio trascorso sotto la guida di Pep Guardiola: “Ci vuole un po' di tempo, ma in generale sono contento”. La priorità resta quella di trovare il giusto compromesso tra la produzione offensiva e la solidità difensiva. Il Napoli, invece, può tornare a concentrarsi sul campionato con rinnovato entusiasmo: domenica c'è il Sassuolo, un appuntamento che Allegri ha già indicato come particolarmente delicato sotto il profilo mentale.
