All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • It has been revealed that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

It has been revealed that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 newly introduced players, but did not upgrade two of the most important positions on the pitch.

In a recent development, only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the massive difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Recent findings suggest that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Industry observers note that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Recent findings suggest that asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

In a recent development, “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he remarked: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

In a recent development, jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

It has been revealed that johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery mentioned. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

Industry observers note that “Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia reveals his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

“We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we revealed a really good character.”.

It has been revealed that and that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Recent findings suggest that callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Recent findings suggest that though Savio takes the corner promptly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

In a recent development, maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

It has been revealed that kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

Sources indicate that the Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

According to recent reports, this is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Recent findings suggest that gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

Sources indicate that villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Sources indicate that tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his upcoming club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

It has been revealed that he gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

So close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

In a recent development, huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Industry observers note that ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being quickly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

In a recent development, but the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Industry observers note that savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

We’re back in action in north London.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus.

Villa: Wan-Bissaka for Matty Cash.

Industry observers note that and as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

According to recent reports, johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

According to recent reports, it looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

Possession: Spurs 57% vs 44% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 14 vs 11.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:.

Zion Suzuki with a double save to deny Spurs an opener 🧤📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/b7WITUtjf2.

Recent findings suggest that back-to-back huge saves from Zion Suzuki! 🤯📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/uXKkicEeer.

Industry observers note that predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

According to recent reports, boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

It has been revealed that well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Recent findings suggest that robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

Van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Mings makes the run looking to get his head on it, but van de Ven goes up with him and gets there first to clear it, though the Dutch international takes a blow to the head and goes down for treatment.

Joao Gomes races forward, sending the ball to Ruggeri on his left. He tries to put it in the box, but it goes out the back off Archie Gray for Villa’s first corner.

McGinn delivers but it comes off Solanke, who clears. No luck yet as we head towards half-time, despite plenty of action in front of goal.

Roberston again with a sliding cross that Lindelof sends out the back.

Industry observers note that another corner for Spurs, but it is headed away again by Mings, who gets up high. That’s Spurs’s seventh corner.

Great long ball from Robertson to try and find Marmoush but Suzuki comes far outside his area to control it with his chest on the bounce and play it away with his feet.

It has been revealed that villa get a free kick inside as Bentancur catches Manzambi, but the Swiss international goes down and receives some treatment on the pitch. He has to go off for a minute, but he is on his feet.

Recent findings suggest that but Spurs come again and it’s Tonali this time. He takes a shot from outside the area, and would have beaten Suzuki low on the right, but the shot is just wide.

Spurs get a corner, delivered by Savio, and it’s headed on to Solanke at the back post. He heads it towards goal but it’s blocked by Wan-Bissaka. Cries for handball, but it’s cleared.

Marmoush makes a very well-timed run to get on a long ball from van Hecke, and does well to stay onside. But his first touch is not good enough and Suzuki can come to collect.

Jackson picks up a ball from Kamara, played over him into the Spurs half. He puts it into the centre of the field towards Buendia, who tees up Manzambi but his shot from distance sails over the bar.

According to recent reports, villa now having a spell. Manzambi gets onto a loose ball in midfield and lays it off to Buendia who feeds Jackson in the centre of the field. He does well to keep the ball down and turn round van Hecke to take a shot on the edge of the area, but he skews his shot wide.

He should be hitting the target at least from there but you can see how desperate both sides are to get their noses in front here.

Jackson gets around Gray and runs into the box on the left side. He pokes a ball through to Buendia, who takes a shot on goal at the near post, but Kinsky gets down to his left to stop the shot.

Industry observers note that mings almost causes a catastrophe for Villa as he and Lindelof close a loose ball down. Suzuki comes out to claim, but the defender pokes it towards him, almost past him under pressure and the keeper has to send it out the sideline.

It has been revealed that four huge saves by Suzuki as Spurs have had five early shots in total to Villa’s single shot on target. They are finding a lot of joy against the left side of Villa’s defence.

Fernandes has an attempt from distance, but drags his shot wide.

Well Spurs are really pushing for a goal!

Recent findings suggest that it’s a perfect first involvement for Gray, as he times a perfect run to get behind Ruggeri to pick up a ball from Savio. He lets it run inside the box but it flashes across the face of goal, just tipped away by Suzuki.

Another attempt denied immediately after as Savio connects perfectly with the volley on the edge of the area, and Suzuki dives down to his left to parry away.

Incredible start for the Villa keeper and Spurs can smell a goal coming.

Spurs had started on the front foot, but let’s see how they handle this change.

Porro went straight down the tunnel when he went off. It was a problem with his left leg. That’s a blow for Spurs, as Porro offers an attacking threat.

According to recent reports, early concern for Spurs as Porro has gone down and is looking very frustrated. Archie Gray has gone out to warm up, but this is a huge blow for De Zerbi if Porro has to come off.

Industry observers note that he had been missing due to a muscle injury but it’s not clear if that’s the matter here. He has been very good so far today, helping build play and bringing huge amounts of experience.

And a shot on target next for Villa as Manzambi has an effort from just inside the 18-yard box off his left foot, but Kinsky makes a relatively easy save as the ball boucnes towards him.

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

No wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Outstanding from the Villa keeper!

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Sums up the early battles so far.

Industry observers note that spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

Sources indicate that savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

Villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

And we are underway in north London!

Industry observers note that watch for some long balls from Tyrone Mings down the channels for Nicolas Jackson today. The pair had a little chat before kick-off with Jackson seemingly telling Mings where he wants the ball released to.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Both teams are coming out of the tunnel now, greeted with plenty of noise from the home and away fans.

The stakes are very high for a match so early on the season and kick-off here we come!

This is the second fixture of the week, as Brentford stormed past Chelsea last night 3-0.

Coming up this weekend for you:.

An early goal here for Villa could be catastrophic for the home team.

Neither club have had any players called up for England, but plenty of players will be leaving to join up with their national teams abroad.

Recent findings suggest that from Spurs, Pedro Porro has retained his place in Spain’s squad. Both Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke have been called up for the Netherlands and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky will join the Czech Republic squad, still awaiting his first senior cap.

Among the Villa players to receive call-ups, Johan Manzambi will be leaving to join the Switzerland squad, while captain John McGinn has been called up for Scotland once again. Zion Suzuki will leave to join Japan in the three-week break as well.

No Mathys Tel in the Spurs squad. De Zerbi has given him plenty of chances, but Tel has always been one of the first players the head coach has criticised this season.

In a recent development, “We have to improve in everything, because like I said, after the game we conceded the first goal in a bad way, because we knew what was the initiative in the defensive phase. One long ball on Gakpo is not enough to concede a goal. Also the second goal could have closed Gakpo better and stronger, and the third goal is an individual skill of Szoboszlai.

It has been revealed that “We can improve in the qualities of the play. I think we created more chances than the other games, also because Liverpool played with more courage.

“There was more space to attack, to make one-to-one, but I have experience enough to say that sometimes when you are the coach of the team, without you knowing the reason, you are able to score, you can score. And other times, another situation where I think you are playing well, not fantastic, but well enough to score, enough to win, and you don’t win.

According to recent reports, “You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence. We move on and we keep going to be better day by day, but not by words, but by fact.”.

It has been revealed that “Similar, like us, but their potential is a huge potential. They signed, spending, a lot of very good players, but they need as well, time to get compact everything and to achieve understanding their idea.

Industry observers note that “Of course, (Roberto) De Zerbi, he’s a fantastic manager. He played fantastic football here and performed fantastic here in Brighton. He did a fantastic job before as well, in Shakhtar, and in Italy, and after Brighton, a fantastic job in Marseille.

“And now, when I can watch them, they are in this process, but of course, they are getting better, they compete fantastic, even losing against Liverpool.

“Of course, being very, very demanding defensively for us, trying to impose and dominate our moment with the ball as well during the game. This is the challenge. Of course, Tottenham, I expect them to be in the top four.”.

Sources indicate that two changes for Villa from the side that lost to Nottingham Forest, with Johan Manzambi and Joao Gomes entering the mix. It’s a first full debut for Manzambi since joining the club from Freiburg over the summer. Gomes returns having served his suspension following a red card against Brighton on the opening weekend.

Representing Aston Villa ✊ pic.twitter.com/5xnjiPnRny.

Industry observers note that only one change from the team that faced Everton, as Pedro Porro returns to the starting XI, replacing Archie Gray. Carabao Cup goal-scorer Connor Gallagher is on the bench.

Our Spurs side to face Villa 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Xgpl4Hx9VV.

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side presently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

In a recent development, tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

According to recent reports, but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

In a recent development, dopo la paura, tanta voglia di vivere, giocare e ritornare a segnare: Yael Trepy, attaccante francese del Cagliari, a metà agosto aveva rischiato di annegare in un giorno di vacanza in una villa vicino a Baja Sardinia, in Gallura. Poi la terapia intensiva, il coma farmacologico, il risveglio.

It has been revealed that da alcune settimane è di nuovo nel gruppo ed è tornato in campo con la Lazio. E ha pure rischiato di fare gol. Questo pomeriggio ha ricevuto il premio Ussi per la rete dell'esordio nello scorso campionato a Cremona.

In a recent development, "Non era sicuramente la mia ora - ha detto a margine della consegna del riconoscimento - tante le persone che hanno pregato per me, che hanno voluto che io non fuggissi da questo mondo. Ci penso ancora, sì. Però ormai è una cosa che è passata". I messaggi più belli? "Quelli di mio fratello - ha ricordato - e del mister: lui (Pisacane è stato in coma a 14 anni per la sindrome di Guillain-Barré, ndr) sa come ci si sente e mi ha detto di non mollare. Ma tutti mi sono stati vicini: la società, i compagni, i tifosi. Con i tifosi ora sento che c'è un legame speciale".

"Il campo mi era mancato tanto - ha osservato - perché diciamo che il calcio è la mia vita, è il mio mestiere e stare fuori per tanti mesi è stata dura. Forse ho scoperto qualcosa di me che non conoscevo, non entro nel dettaglio".

Adesso è pronto anche a segnare:.

"Mi sento sempre meglio - ha spiegato - Poi ovviamente ci saranno altre partite per continuare a crescere. È ovvio che a ogni partita penso al gol, però questo è un obiettivo più personale che per il gruppo".

"Dobbiamo affrontare questo impegno come con le altre squadre, sempre per vincere anche perché giochiamo in casa - ha sostenuto - la differenza di punti con le altre grandi non si è sentita: possiamo giocarcela".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that È un Francesco Totti che parla a cuore aperto, quello presente negli studi di Rai 2 ospite del programma "Belve" condotto da Francesca Fagnani. La conduttrice ha incalzato l'ex capitano della Roma - nello spirito e col timing tipico del format - portandolo tra una gaffe e l'altra su tantissimi temi non strettamente legati al mondo del pallone.

"Lei ha detto di non poter fare l'allenatore perché troppo buono...", una delle domande della Fagnani che trova subito conferma nella risposta di Totti: "Quando sei dall'altra parte è tutto più semplice. Mettendomi nella posizione dell'allenatore che deve scegliere per forza 11 giocatori, mi dispiacerebbe non farli giocare tutti…". Non manca spazio all'ironia che ha da sempre (o quasi) contraddistinto Totti: "Prima ero molto più rosicone. Poi Maurizio Costanzo mi fece cambiare idea, invitandomi al suo programma e dicendomi di essere più autoironico, di non prendermela per quello che dicevano. Da quel giorno mi è cambiata la prospettiva in meglio".

Dopo aver dato una spiegazione alla sua popolarità che va oltre quella di una normale persona famosa ("Forse è l'amore che ho dato a questa città, non l'ho mai tradita e mai gli ho girato le spalle"), Totti affronta anche il filone legato alla Roma: "Nel 2004 potevo andare a Madrid. La testa lo voleva ma il cuore no. Alla fine è stata la decisione più giusta. Al Real avrei vinto di più. Il Pallone d'Oro? Col Real avrei avuto più possibilità, con la Roma era più difficile".

Inevitabile tornare sull'addio alla Roma. Fagnani chiede: cosa cambierebbe del finale per renderlo meno doloroso? Totti risponde senza pensarci troppo: "Avrei cambiato il modo di comportarsi della società nei miei confronti. Avrei preferito che mi rispettassero di più dopo quello che ho fatto. Ho lottato fino a sei mesi prima che finisse, a dicembre ho mollato mentalmente per quello che stavo ricevendo da persone che non mi sarei mai aspettato".

Sources indicate that E dopo l'addio al calcio? "Una mini depressione - continua Totti - , mi ero chiuso in me stesso. Poi gli amici e i familiari mi hanno aiutato. Tra i miei amici nel mondo del calcio mi hanno aiutato molto Candela e Vito Scala".

Qualcuno si è mai approfittato della sua posizione? "Diciamo persone impensabili, persone molto vicine a me, familiari, amici, parenti. Brutto dirlo ma hanno mangiato abbastanza un po' tutti, però non rinnego niente. Alla fine l'ho fatto col cuore e la generosità. Poi però passa il tempo, le strade si dividono capisci quello che è successo realmente in quei momenti".

Sources indicate that tornare alla Roma? "Non so più che dire. Quando sarà, se succederà, lo saprete. La porta on si chiude mai a nessuno, ma in questo momento io e la Roma abbiamo percorsi diversi, io sto bene e loro stanno facendo un grande lavoro. O si parte da zero o non si parte. Ma non è nessun messaggio".

Dopo il pari del Napoli per 2-2 contro il Manchester, Giovane ha parlato così in mixed zone:.

“Noi sapevamo che era una partita difficile oggi, il Manchester City è una delle migliori squadre del mondo, quindi il mister ha parlato con tutti noi per entrare con la testa giusta e fare una buona prestazione. È un peccato che abbiamo pareggiato, però è un punto importante per perseguire i nostri obiettivi. Penso che noi abbiamo fatto una buona gara, una buona prestazione. Adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti perché domenica c’è un’altra partita in Serie A. Adesso è già finita e dobbiamo pensare avanti. Qualunque sia il modulo tattico con cui giochiamo, sappiamo quello che dobbiamo fare. Ovviamente si cambia qualcosa quando si cambia modulo, ma penso che anche l’ultima vittoria ci abbia aiutato a prendere fiducia per affrontare oggi questa partita. Giocare qui è difficilissimo perché il Manchester City è una squadra forte. Sappiamo che adesso stanno attraversando un momento difficile, ma non smettono di essere il Manchester City e anche noi non smettiamo di essere il Napoli, quindi è questo. La risposta è quella di sempre, che noi abbiamo quella voglia, quella fame, quella grinta di vincere, è questo. Speriamo che domenica possiamo vincere. Sì, può essere, perché se vinciamo e conquistiamo tre punti così cambia tutto, però anche un punto in una partita come quella di questa sera è importante. La Champions è una competizione difficile, ma adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti e perseguire i nostri obiettivi”.

It has been revealed that intervenuto ai microfoni di Radiosei, Fabio Liverani ha commentato il grande inizio di stagione della Lazio. Dopo dodici giornate la squadra di Gattuso è sorprendentemente in testa alla classifica. "Ad oggi la parola ‘scudetto’ è difficile da pronunciare per tante cose, se pensi da dove sei partito, se guardi la rosa di altre squadre. Però parlare del ‘quarto posto’ credo sia lecito, non sarà semplice ma la Lazio ha dimostrato sul campo che si può pensare a questo. La Lazio deve competere sempre per l’Europa, dalla Conference in sù. Dalla Conference in giù, per la Lazio, la stagione è sempre negativa. Tra due mesi analizzeremo quello che sarà, ad oggi credo si possa giocare per la Champions League”.

“Discorso Champions, c’è da temere più il Milan o il Como? Io il Como lo vedo dentro le prime quattro, è una squadra che difficilmente può toppare con le medio-piccole, il Milan sta risalendo ma ancora il Como lo vedo favorito. Il presidente rossonero comunque ci ha messo la faccia e questo conta, quindi a gennaio sicuramente farà qualcosa. Il Milan lo vedo in miglioramento ma ancora in una fase di costruzione, è chiaro che il mercato di gennaio può spostare gli equilibri. Il Como ha un’identità. Inter, Lazio, Roma e Como difficilmente possono perdere tanti punti con le squadre della parte destra. Milan e Juventus non mi danno questa certezza con le ‘piccole’".

Bruno Fernandes reveals contract negotiations with Manchester United have stalled after he rejected a fresh deal in the summer

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed latest deal.
  • The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed latest deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

It has been revealed that 'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United.

'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always highlighted how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

Sources indicate that 'And I've always remarked the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club indicates "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a fresh contract so I think that from their side shows that they want me to stay.

Industry observers note that 'As I noted there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most vital thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'.

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a major-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

According to recent reports, united presently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he notes in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he mentioned.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'.

Recent findings suggest that his post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

Recent findings suggest that 'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he remarked. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference.

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

It has been revealed that 'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

Industry observers note that 'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'.

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

Luciano Spalletti grida e chiede un centravanti ma l'operato di Giovanni Carnevali, Frederic Massara e di Marco Ottolini è già ben chiaro da tempo. Un centravanti non può cadere dal cielo, perché ci sono problemi di lista, di conti e di rosa da considerare.

Recent findings suggest that la Juventus vuole un 9 ma per questioni di lista in caso di arrivo di un giocatore straniero, deve cederne uno straniero. La Juventus ha ancora a disposizione 1 slot per tesserare un calciatore extracomunitario proveniente dall'estero in questa stagione, ma non può inserirlo nella lista Serie A senza prima liberare un posto nella lista dei 17 "Over 22" non formati in Italia. In a recent development, non solo: Anche se il club può formalmente tesserare un nuovo extracomunitario, il regolamento della Serie A impone un limite massimo di 25 giocatori in rosa, di cui solo 17 liberi da vincoli di formazione. La Juventus ha tutti e 17 questi slot già pieni, al punto da aver dovuto escludere calciatori come Arkadiusz Milik e Khephren Thuram, e potrà effettuare al massimo 2 sostituzioni di giocatori di movimento nel corso dell'intera stagione. E il francese verrà reintegrato in rosa, per questo uno dovrà uscire. Chi? L'indiziato numero uno è Teun Koopmeiners, che a gennaio peserà a bilancio per 25,8 milioni di euro e ne guadagna 5,77 lordi a stagione. Come già detto e ribadito in passato: al momento dell'acquisto, c'era la fila delle squadre in Italia e in Europa per prenderlo, poi l'olandese non è riuscito ad adattarsi (ma l'impressione che possa tornare grande altrove...). Cederlo a queste cifre sarà dura, ma per rimetter dentro Thuram, e verrà fatto, uno dovrà essere tolto dalla lista.

Sources indicate that A questo si lega dunque la questione del terzino. Vuoi un 'Alejandro Baldé'? Deve partire Juan Cabal. Altrimenti un italiano per Andrea Cambiaso, semplice. E lo stesso in attacco. Certo, dovesse arrivare Gianluca Scamacca dall'Atalanta, lì davanti potrebbe partire Edon Zhegrova (indiziato ma anche lì, mica facile), e allora andrebbe bene anche cedere Cambiaso per prendere un terzino. Insomma, l'intreccio è chiaro (ma complicato) e in questo la Juventus deve anche rientrare nei paletti del settlement agreement. Tanti fattori, adesso sta camminando su un sottile filo e gli investimenti a gennaio sembrano da escludere a meno di una maxi cessione.

Industry News: Kim Hellberg indicates Middlesbrough ‘absolutely’ need to strengthen key position in the January transfer window

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that and, the Boro boss mentioned that the midfield is an area that needs to be bolstered.
  • Speaking to The Northern Echo, Hellberg remarked: “So, if you look at all those things, of course we need to strengthen that in January, absolutely.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, middlesbrough are flying high in the Championship, with Saturday’s victory over Bristol City moving them top of the table. Ahead of Tuesday’s clash with Swansea City though, potential January transfer window reinforcements were on Kim Hellberg’s mind.

Industry observers note that and, the Boro boss mentioned that the midfield is an area that needs to be bolstered. His statement comes after a long-term hamstring injury to Rokas Pukstas, while Connor Barron is out of favour and also dealing with an injury problem of his own.

Speaking to The Northern Echo, Hellberg remarked: “So, if you look at all those things, of course we need to strengthen that in January, absolutely.”.

Hellberg is right in saying that a upcoming midfielder is an absolute must for Middlesbrough. The injury to Pukstas and Barron’s absence and lack of favour mean that the Boro boss’ options in the middle of the park have dwindled significantly.

Sources indicate that however, whoever joins has a tough battle on their hands to get into the team. American teammates Aidan Morris and Sebastian Berhalter have forged an excellent partnership in the first third of the campaign, and they are going to prove tough to dislodge.

Riley McGree can drop into a deeper role if needs be, but he is at his best in a more attacking role. The same goes for Myles Peart-Harris, so a defence-minded midfielder would bring more balance and depth to the department.

The player signed will have to be up for the fight to break into the team though. They may also have to accept that starting opportunities could be somewhat limited, with Morris and Berhalter among the Championship’s best performers of the season to date.

Middlesbrough spent substantial in the summer, with much of the funds going towards reinforcements in attack and defence. Will Lankshear and Ashley Phillips joined from Spurs for sizeable fees, and a package deal worth £14m was struck for Radek Vitek.

Berhalter, Peart-Harris and Pukstas joined as new midfielders. But of those, Boro’s new American star Berhalter cost less than £900,000 up front, and Peart-Harris was signed on a free transfer.

Despite the busy summer transfer window, it is clear that a newly introduced midfielder is needed. Boro can not afford to rest on their laurels in the Championship promotion push, with a deep and talented squad needed to deal with the rigours of a 46-game league season.

At least one midfielder – preferably a defence-first one – could help push Hellberg and co over the line after last season’s Championship play-off heartbreak.

Industry News: Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

  • Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

Sources indicate that 'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'.

Recent findings suggest that asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with.

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

Sources indicate that you make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

It has been revealed that there has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate.

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Recent findings suggest that spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Scorers: Williams-Barnett, Solanke.

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

In a recent development, belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' said Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'.

It has been revealed that spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Sources indicate that savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

Industry observers note that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

In a recent development, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

It has been revealed that “It was a really good fight,” Alisson noted, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

According to recent reports, since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola stated. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

According to recent reports, don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

According to recent reports, isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Industry observers note that cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Recent findings suggest that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Industry observers note that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

Sources indicate that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose remarked. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola stated: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that revealed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

According to recent reports, "Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

"That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

Cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young mentioned on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose massive players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Industry observers note that andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Industry observers note that everything Iraola has remarked and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Sources indicate that adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He remarked: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

It has been revealed that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his massive move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Recent findings suggest that liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham sold the midfielder to the Belgian side in the last transfer window. WHUFC gave their academy graduate the green light to head out the exit door on a permanent basis.

Potts, 23, penned a long-term contract with Club Brugge running until June 2030. He has made 16 appearances in all competitions since his move abroad, four of which have come in the Champions League, and he has chipped in with one assist.

In a recent development, he has opened up about his exit from the London Stadium on BBC Radio 5 Live’s Euro Leagues Show: “In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren’t as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and remarked ‘let’s explore options because this season I’m 22, turning 23’. It’s a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn’t really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

“I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career. It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite swiftly. It’s been the right decision for me and so far I’m enjoying it, I’m loving life here.”.

According to recent reports, west Ham are well stocked up with options in Potts’ position. WHUFC have the likes of Arne Engels, Divine Mukasa, Edson Alvarez and Tomas Soucek, among others, at their disposal.

In a recent development, therefore, Potts wouldn’t have played many minutes for the Hammers this season. His decision to leave for Club Brugge has worked out well for him so far.

Industry observers note that the Barking-born man has become a key player for his current club. He is also getting exposure to European football which will do him good.

Sources indicate that potts rose up through West Ham’s ranks and was a regular for them at various different youth levels as a youngster. He was loaned out to Wycombe Wanderers and Portsmouth in the EFL to get some experience under his belt and to boost his development.

It has been revealed that he made his first-team debut for the Hammers back in 2021 in a Europa League clash against Dinamo Zagreb. He went on to make a further 32 outings for the London outfit, 25 of which came in the last campaign.

Potts has settled into life at Club Brugge with relative ease. His side take on Liverpool at home in the Champions League on Wednesday night and they are 2nd in their league table behind Royale Union Saint-Gilloise.

It has been revealed that west Ham will be disappointed to have seen him depart but they couldn’t offer him consistent minutes anymore due to too much competition for places. The Hammers have seen their form in the Championship slump over recent weeks.

In a recent development, they have recently turned to Scott Parker as their new manager but the ex-Fulham and Burnley man has struggled to make an impact so far. His side drew 1-1 at home against Preston North End last time out and couldn’t find a winner.

When building a squad it is important to have a vision of the end goal, and AC Milan have exactly that heading into 2027.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by stating that there are no transition years when it comes to Milan. Frequently they have chosen to overhaul the squad in the summer window, and sometimes even in the winter.

Industry observers note that for example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

Industry observers note that the Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

Recent findings suggest that the difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

In a recent development, A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

According to recent reports, then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Recent findings suggest that milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

It’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the upcoming Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

It has been revealed that the idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to strategy. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

Industry observers note that the former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

In a recent development, belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

💡 Key Takeaways
