  • Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.
  • Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026.

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title.

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched.

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021.

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sheffield United face Southampton in the Championship tonight.
  • Recent findings suggest that SUFC have lost one of their last six league matches, and at Bramall Lane, they’ll be eager to give the promotion-pushing Saints a good test.
  • Tanganga picked up his fifth booking of the season in the Watford victory and will serve his one-match suspension against Southampton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield United face Southampton in the Championship tonight. The Blades come into the game in good form, having defeated Watford 4-0 on Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that SUFC have lost one of their last six league matches, and at Bramall Lane, they’ll be eager to give the promotion-pushing Saints a good test. However, Chris Wilder will have to undo a 17-year hoodoo to do so, and he’ll be without captain and key defender Japhet Tanganga for the tie.

Tanganga picked up his fifth booking of the season in the Watford victory and will serve his one-match suspension against Southampton. It means that 25-year-old Mark McGuinness is set to be recalled to the Sheffield United starting XI as they look for a first league point against the South Coast side since 2009.

Sources indicate that mcGuinness was touted for a move away from Bramall Lane in the summer, but he ended up staying put. He’s had a part to play at Sheffield United despite the past uncertainty too, starting seven Championship games so far this term.

However, summer signing Liam Kitching has become the preferred centre-back partner for skipper Tanganga. That partnership has been increasingly impressive, providing a solid defensive foundation for SUFC to build on in their improved form of late.

In a recent development, but, barring a surprise call to start Jamal Baptiste for the first time since September 19th, it will be McGuinness who lines up against Southampton. The Irishman will hope his strong aerial presence and no-nonsense, box-guarding defensive style can help keep the Saints and their dangerous attackers at bay.

The likely partnership of McGuinness and Kitching will have to deal with the fit-again Cyle Larin, who scored on his return to the side against Derby County on Saturday. The Canadian international now has nine goals to his name in 14 games across all competitions this season.

Sheffield United are in for a tough task tonight, there can be no illusions over that.

Southampton have history on their side in this fixture with six consecutive league wins over the Blades since 2009. The last time SUFC were triumphant in this fixture, a late goal from Jamie Ward secured a 2-1 triumph at St Mary’s.

Recent findings suggest that 17 years on, the Saints are under Tonda Eckert‘s lead and pushing for Championship promotion. They sit 6th in the table, but would be 3rd if it wasn’t for their four-point deduction as part of the Spygate saga.

In a recent development, the visitors are the favourites, but they are not invincible away from home – far from it, in fact. Southampton have won two, drawn three and lost three of their eight league matches on the road this term, so SUFC certainly have an opening there.

McGuinness will have to step up and fill Tanganga’s shoes to deal with Larin and the rest of the Saints’ attacking threats. If they can do so, Sheffield United might just pull off an impressive win on Tuesday night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hundreds of millions of people around the world are affected by diabetes mellitus1. It develops when the activity of insulin, a glucose-lowering hormone secreted by pancreatic β-cells, becomes insufficient to maintain healthy glucose levels in the blood. The condition can be managed with oral medication or by injecting insulin and other metabolic hormones, but the constant need for people with diabetes to manage their lifestyle and blood-glucose levels can impair their quality of life. Therapeutic approaches that monitor and control blood glucose automatically are therefore highly desirable. Writing in Nature, Xiu et al.2 report proof of principle of a bioelectronic device called NeuroAxis that does exactly that in rat models of diabetes.

Published: 11:18 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026.

Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have confirmed they're expecting their first child together.

The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours.

It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news.

It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece.

Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby.

Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift'.

Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000.

According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano.

There, McTominay can be by the seaside swiftly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre.

The couple regularly share photos from their newly introduced life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in major moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

This season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday.

McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test.

The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino.

He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights.

The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly.

'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'.

  • "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville indicates Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

Industry observers note that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville indicates Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

In a recent development, neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

Sources indicate that it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the blueprint to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

Industry observers note that we now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

Sources indicate that that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

Industry observers note that it is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

According to recent reports, the goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It has been revealed that it was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

It has been revealed that "A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

Fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their new head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

United’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

Recent findings suggest that but, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Sources indicate that might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

It has been revealed that I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

According to recent reports, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville states Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

In a recent development, I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

Recent findings suggest that I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

In a recent development, we wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Recent findings suggest that now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so important for us.

According to recent reports, there were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

Industry observers note that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

Sources indicate that I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

Recent findings suggest that it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

Industry observers note that it was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

It has been revealed that the defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

In a recent development, 5 - With five points, this is Manchester United's joint-lowest tally after five games of a Premier League season, also picking up five in 2014-15.Sluggish. pic.twitter.com/UZTBWRpGnm.

Fulham remain winless but the draw lifts them above Spurs, who will spend the international break at the foot of the table. It is just one win in five for United, and it was another performance which was far from convincing. It could have been worse though, they were a few minutes away from losing. On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Fulham wanted a free-kick on the edge of the box for a sliding challenge on Kevin for Maguire but the referee decides he got the ball.

United break forward and win a corner. It comes for Martinez who shifts his feet to shoot with his right foot and the goal-bound effort was blocked!

Just the three minutes of added time to play, but United are the team pushing forward searching for an unlikely winner.

United may have just spared themselves a damaging defeat, and there might just be time to go on an win this. Cunha with a speculative shot from outside the box, and Affengruber extends his left leg to block the shot but the deflection leaves Leno stranded. A stroke of luck for United but Fulham have invited it.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

Bassey now penalised for a high boot on Dalot, United free-kick on the halfway line. Fulham just about standing firm, and they are helped when a crossfield pass towards Dorgu bounces off for a throw-in.

United with another corner and there are loud appeals for a handball penalty against Bassey, the proximity was very close but his hand was up. But VAR takes a look and the fact the hand was tucked in towards his chest spares the Fulham defender.

Fulham and the home crowd happy with a goal kick after an overhit cross towards Shaw at the back post. Dorgu has been sent on in Carrick’s last throw of the dice, replacing Shaw at left-back.

You would not say United are pulling Fulham from pillar to post, it feels a little hopeful, but it is one-way traffic. An attack against defence session in Fulham’s half. Charles and Kevin do well to relieve the pressure momentarily, but United are back on the attack again.

Sources indicate that here are those changes: Mason Mount on for Kobbie Mainoo for United, while Andersen replaces King for the home team. Arbeloa happy to hold what he has. Lisandro Martinez volleys a shot over the bar.

Positive first involvement from Zirkzee, releasing Mbeumo, but the Fulham defenders read his intentions and blocked the shot after he cut inside. Joachim Andersen is preparing to come on for Fulham, as is Mason Mount for United.

Recent findings suggest that much better from Fulham, another attack started by Bassey reading play just like the goal, but this time Lammens’s wrists were strong to parry Kevin’s shot. Rashford is then flagged offside.

According to recent reports, fulham change: Larsson is on for Berge, Sweden for Norway. And Carrick has brought on Zirkzee for Rashford. Famous last words, but does that make you more likely to score a goal? Not that Rashford can feel hard done to.

Fulham have stopped playing since they scored, and they needed Leno again to tip a Cunha shot around the post. The United forward was falling over, but he generated enough power to trouble the goalkeeper. From the corner, Maguire picks up the ball on the far side and chips a cross over the blue shirts in the middle.

Kevin sold himself in a one-on-one with Rashford, but King did well to put his foot in at the edge of the box and the ball bounces through kindly to Leno. Tielemans then misplaces a pass when United were in a promising position.

If United had played like this from the start of the second half they would not be losing, but now they have just 20 minutes plus stoppage time to overturn the deficit.

Fulham making a double sub: Kevin and Palacios on for Iwobi and Bobb.

United have roused themselves since conceding, winning a flurry of corners.

What a save from Leno! Mbeumo’s curling shot from outside the box was arcing beautifully into the far corner, but the German goalkeeper tipped his effort around the post.

Then Maguire is eased out at the back post, and Fulham breathe a sigh of relief.

Strong words from Gary Neville after the goal went it: “I’ve watched United since the age of five and that is the worst 15 minutes [from half-time to the goal] I have seen them play.”.

Well doesn’t that just sum up United’s season so far. There are appeals for a foul on Cunha from Bassey, but the Fulham defender was stronger and he took some initiative to drive towards the box. Bassey let fly and kept his shot down, Lammens could only stick out a leg and the ball rebounded off the helpless Martinez and back into the net.

In a recent development, "A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

Industry observers note that fulham have a corner after it opened up nicely for Iwobi at the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike deflects behind. A very smooth footballer, but finishing has never been Iwobi’s strong suit. Fulham fail to make anything of the corner.

Fulham and United’s fans now urging their teams on after the game halted to glacial pace. Nothing much happening at all since the start of the second half.

Industry observers note that gary Neville growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of intensity out of possession by both teams: “Never walk on a football pitch.” Questions have been asked of United’s fitness levels and physical readiness for the new season. Fulham enjoying a spell of possession in United’s half again.

More from Neville: “It’s like it’s time for the whites to play against the blue mannequins, before they reverse it up the other end. One thing I do know, I’ve played in a lot of football matches, it’s not right.”.

There has been a real lack of conviction in Rashford’s play in the final third, this time it was underhit pass across the box towards Mbeumo which was cut out. Good ball by Tielemans to release Rashford, but no end product again.

Sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

Fulham kick off in the second half.

It has been revealed that at half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

It has been revealed that united almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

Recent findings suggest that united’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

It has been revealed that cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

In a recent development, mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

Sources indicate that this stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

Recent findings suggest that fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

Recent findings suggest that fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

It has been revealed that the interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

In a recent development, fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Recent findings suggest that bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

Industry observers note that A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

According to recent reports, fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Industry observers note that promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

Industry observers note that if Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

Subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

Here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

It has been revealed that the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a massive impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager noted.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty substantial one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

Sources indicate that “But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty substantial one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he noted it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

Industry observers note that the mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and fresh head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

It has been revealed that fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

Sheffield Wednesday must deal with Stevenage’s ageless danger man to secure a third consecutive win under Dave Challinor

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, sheffield Wednesday have rediscovered winning form in League One since the arrival of Dave Challinor.
  • Sources indicate that next up for Challinor and the Owls is Stevenage on Tuesday night.
  • It will be a tricky test for Sheffield Wednesday, and the key to picking up a third League One win on the trot will be keeping Boro striker Josh Magennis quiet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, sheffield Wednesday have rediscovered winning form in League One since the arrival of Dave Challinor. The newly introduced SWFC boss oversaw a 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle before a battling triumph at Oakwell against Barnsley.

Sources indicate that next up for Challinor and the Owls is Stevenage on Tuesday night. Boro have had an inconsistent season, leaving them in 14th as they look to build on last term’s play-off finish. Alex Revell’s side are a tough one, with physical players across the pitch.

It will be a tricky test for Sheffield Wednesday, and the key to picking up a third League One win on the trot will be keeping Boro striker Josh Magennis quiet. At 36, the Northern Irishman has been one of the standout performers at Broadhall Way this season.

In a recent development, magennis moved to Stevenage in the summer after the expiry of his contract at relegated Exeter City. He maintained a consistent output with the Grecians, recording 21 goals in 89 games for the club as he plays well into his 30s.

According to recent reports, and, he’s been a hugely effective player for Revell’s Boro too. Magennis has always been a physical presence at the top of the pitch, and the 6ft 2in striker is perfect for Stevenage. His strength and ability in the air make him a real outlet at the top of the pitch and from crossing or set-piece situations.

Not only do these attributes make him a goalscoring threat, but Magennis’ ability to win knock-downs or hold up the ball for his teammates makes him a creative asset too. If Sheffield Wednesday can’t contain him, the Bangor-born striker will be key in tonight’s game.

Recent findings suggest that compared with his fellow League One strikers, no one has created more goalscoring opportunities than Magennis’ 19 – six of them big chances. He wins 48% of his aerial duels and 44.4% of his duels overall (stats via FotMob).

Sources indicate that magennis is in some of the most productive form of his career. He is a perfect fit for Stevenage’s style of play, and it is helping him age like a fine wine and contribute in the twilight of his career.

Dealing with Magennis’ presence is not easy – his recent League One opponents will tell you that.

However, Sheffield Wednesday do have the personnel to limit his impact. In Liam Cooper, Challinor has a vastly experienced centre-back who will be wise to Magennis’ tricks and style, and he can be key in preventing the Stevenage man from having his way while guiding his fellow defenders on how to deal with him too.

Sources indicate that of the potential starters, it may be Cooper and Sil Swinkels tasked with challenging Magennis in the air. They have aerial duel win rates of 72.6% and 73.3% respectively this season, while Di’Shon Bernard has a lower but respectable 68% (FotMob).

Recent findings suggest that magennis is usually a lone striker, but with on-rushing attackers in tandem. By suffocating the Boro striker at the source, they can limit his aerial duel wins and prevent him from bringing the ball down to create chances.

It is a task easier remarked than done, but SWFC boss Challinor must have a plan to deal with Magennis if he is to maintain his perfect League One record.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frosinone forward Romano Schmid believes that his side will have to be more ‘proactive’ in order to get a positive result against AC Milan.

Having been promoted from Serie B last season, Frosinone have been the surprise package so far in Serie A barring perhaps the league-leaders Lazio, as they sit sixth in the table having won six of their opening 11 games so far.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

They were heavily tipped to be in a relegation battle by pundits and the bookmakers, and yet they have scored 24 goals and allowed just 15, making them not just an effective team but also an entertaining one too.

The summer arrival Schmid – who signed from Werder Bremen – has been a part of that. He spoke at a press conference two days before Frosinone’s trip north to face Milan at San Siro. The questions and his responses were relayed by TuttoFrosinone.

After Cagliari, what will the match against Milan be like?

“The match in Milan will be completely different from the one in Cagliari. Milan are obviously the favourites, their game is different from Cagliari’s, and we’ll need a more proactive Frosinone.”.

How are you finding Serie A as a league?

Recent findings suggest that “It’s different from the Bundesliga, I like it. You have to always be on top of things otherwise you lose the duels, especially in midfield.”.

Did the fact that they play with a 4-2-3-1 like with Austria influence your choice to come to Frosinone?

“It’s not the main reason. With the national team, we don’t play man-to-man like here against Frosinone. It’s a similar game because we definitely play deep, we attack high.”.

Why did you miss Austria’s last match?

“My son had a problem, it wasn’t serious but he wasn’t feeling very well and since we had already qualified I preferred to stay with the family”.

Industry observers note that you are one of the most important signings in Frosinone’s history, and it’s no coincidence that you started playing immediately under Alvini. How do you feel?

Recent findings suggest that “My past performances in the Bundesliga were crucial; that’s one of the reasons Froisnone chose me, given my previous performances. They’re similar to what I played under coach Alvini. I’m enjoying myself and I’m happy.”.

Where do you prefer to play, in the attacking midfield role or in the pivot?

Industry observers note that “My favourite position is number 10, an attacking midfielder behind the centre-forward. I feel comfortable playing there, I’ve also tried playing further back, but my favourite position is still number 10.”.

It has been revealed that “I haven’t played PlayStation for the last 4-5 years, since I became a father. Last night my wife downloaded the game and we played together.”.

Before kick-off on Sunday, the beneficiaries of the various schemes will take a photo with the starting lineup. “It’s always exciting for me to hear people talk about Franco and what he achieved with these colours, as a player and as a man.

The pregame will also honour the memory of Franco Baresi and his bond with Fondazione Milan. He was a dedicated supporter of its projects, including as a member of its Board of Directors. Club employees will take part in the tribute, along with his longtime teammate and friend Daniele Massaro.

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1263 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts noted enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren.

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time.

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Sources indicate that away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

According to recent reports, the 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

He wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal.

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

Sources indicate that playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

According to recent reports, now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

According to recent reports, arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

It has been revealed that sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

In a recent development, it must be noted that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Industry observers note that yet again, though, they highlighted themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a new thing, either.

It has been revealed that the Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

Sources indicate that they are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

CELTIC (4-3-2-1): Johnstone 6.5; Donovan 7, Carter-Vickers 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Trusty 70); McGregor 7, OXLADE- CHAMBERLAIN 8 (Osmand 60), McCowan 7.5; Yang 7 (Forrest 70), Duran 7 (Mheuka 70); Jota 6.5 (Van den Berg 60). Booked: McCowan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 7.

Recent findings suggest that ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.

Sources indicate that bruno Fernandes is one to watch for the upcoming summer transfer window, with his contract expiring in June 2027 but with an option to extend. United’s attempts to extend his deal have so far been unsuccessful, likely due to the player’s desire to try something else.

Fernandes has played at an incredible level in the Premier League in recent years, winning Player of the Year for 2025-26. So far, he has made 341 official appearances for the Red Devils, scoring 113 goals and providing 111 assists.

It has been revealed that he’s a key player for the Portuguese national team and he would provide leadership that the squad could lose if players like Luka Modric leave. Moreover, his past in Italy – where he had spells at Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria – could help him integrate more rapidly and effectively.

Fernandes also shares the same agency as Ruben Amorim. The relationship between the two is excellent, and already this summer the Rossoneri had inquired about a possible move for the former Sporting star.

At the other Manchester club, however, there’s an old acquaintance of Italian football who could come back into fashion as early as January: Mateo Kovacic. His contract also expires at the end of the campaign, and he could come in to add depth too.

Given the increasingly certain departure of youngster Christian Comotto, an experienced player like Kovacic – at the right price, in terms of wages – could be useful for Amorim. His situation is being watched, but there will be competition from other clubs, likely in Italy too.

Swansea City identify manager with 2.32 points per game as leading contender to replace Vitor Matos

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that swansea City are pursuing a latest head coach after Vitor Matos left his role at the Swansea.com Stadium to take charge of RC Strasbourg.
  • According to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position.
  • Alexandersson is at the moment the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that swansea City are pursuing a latest head coach after Vitor Matos left his role at the Swansea.com Stadium to take charge of RC Strasbourg. Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O’Leary are leading the Swans on an interim basis, but ground is promptly being made in the search for a new boss.

According to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position. Talks have been held between the 44-year-old and the Championship club, and he appears to be their prime target at present.

Alexandersson is at the moment the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June. He has overseen 14 wins in his 19 games in charge of the club, recording a points-per-game rate of 2.32.

Recent findings suggest that alexandersson is a 44-year-old coach who has held a variety of roles in the dugout since beginning his coaching career back in 2008. He spent seven years at Leiknir Reykjavik as a player before moving into management.

The Swansea City target started out in women’s football, managing club team Valur before a short spell in charge of former club Leiknir Reykjavik. Alongside this role, Alexandersson spent five years as manager of the Iceland women’s national side.

He then stepped into the men’s setup as an assistant to Erik Hamren and Arnar Vidarsson before a short spell as a No. 2 at Al-Arabi. From 2021 though, Alexandersson has worked strictly as a first-team boss in men’s football.

He spent nearly three years in charge of Danish side Lyngby BK and 11 months at KV Kortrijk in Belgium before moving to SK Brann in Norway. Impressive work there saw him poached for the Rosenborg BK job, where he has continued to impress.

Swansea City head coach contender Alexandersson prioritises man management, working closely with his players to build strong relationships and placing importance on leadership. He has a strong reputation for developing players, which will appeal to the Swans too.

Tactically, his Rosenborg side set up in a 4-3-3 primarily, but he has used 5-3-2 or 3-5-2 formations in the past. Much like Matos, his teams press aggressively in the final third, and he demands frequent chance creation with players directed to suffocate opponents on and off the ball.

In terms of tactical similarities, Alexandersson feels like a great fit for Swansea City. The fact he wants his players to press high and play forwards much like Matos means that there can be a smooth transition into the new management.

Bringing in a boss with completely different ideas could bring teething problems. This squad has been built to play on the front foot with and without the ball, and Alexandersson will ensure they do so.

The Jamestown Analytics influence feels clear with this pursuit. They pride themselves on finding gems in lesser-used markets, and Alexandersson could be the latest top boss uncovered.

After initial talks, time will tell whether the Swans can strike a deal to bring Alexandersson to Wales.

GdS: Krösche announcement could come next week – how he will operate at Milan

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.
  • La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s prepares.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s prepares.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

Sources indicate that in short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

According to recent reports, krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

It has been revealed that “Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche said upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”.

It has been revealed that the club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”.

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the past few weeks, Ruben Amorim has been battling a long list of absences due to injuries, but how does it compare to one year ago?

Sources indicate that the second international break brings a useful moment to pause and reflect on the injury problems within the squad. Given that there have been at times as many as eight players out, it feels as though Amorim has been rowing against the tide a bit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese asks for a physically demanding style and he consistently emphasises the importance of proper rotation. Yet, at present, the likes of Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Strahinja Pavlovic are all out.

From Stefano Pioli’s final years into Massimiliano Allegri’s one-season stint, there was a recurring problem of muscle problems. For example, last season – despite no European football – the Rossoneri suffered 31 total injuries during the season, leading to a crisis at certain points.

Sources indicate that in the previous season, which included the Champions League, the figure hit 33. In Pioli’s last season in 2023-24, he battled a staggering 40 different issues. How does the current season compare to the last though? MilanNews provide the data.

1. Pulisic – Ankle sprain – July 26 to August 12, 17 days out during the summer. 2. Leao – Right calf elongational injury – August 17 to September 25, 39 days out and missed 5 games. 3. It has been revealed that wolves have handed the winger plenty of game time over the past 12 months or so, despite his tender age. He has become a key member of WWFC’s first-team squad over recent times.

Mane, 19, is under contract at Molineux until the summer of 2029. He has made 18 appearances for the Midlands outfit in all competitions this season, 16 of which have come in the Championship, and he has chipped in with three assists.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on the youngster on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Mane we hold to very high standards because we think he’s a very, very, very good player. It is always worth remembering he only turned 19 two months ago. He’s such a young player still.

“If you look at Championship minutes this season, he’s the second youngest player behind Ryan Kavuma-McQueen to have played more than 600 minutes. He’s in a little bucket there with Kavuma-McQueen, who’s still 17, then Mane and (Divine) Mukasa, who has just turned 19, and then Romelle Donovan, who is just about to turn 20.”.

Wolves will be pleased that they managed to keep hold of Mane over the summer. WWFC were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with West Ham and Burnley.

Industry observers note that mane, who is an ex-England and Portugal youth international, was linked with an exit in the last transfer window. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put beyond the deadline back in early September.

Many expected the teenager to take the second tier by storm but things haven’t exactly panned out like that. He still hasn’t scored and probably hasn’t made the impact in the EFL he would have hoped to before a ball was kicked this term.

Nevertheless, he is starting to find his feet now and is a promising talent. He will get better with experience and his game is still developing.

Industry observers note that mane looked good against Charlton Athletic for Wolves last time out. He caused problems for WWFC’s last opponents and helped them win 2-1 after goals by Adam Armstrong and Rafiki Stated.

Recent findings suggest that cesar Peixoto’s side are back in action on Tuesday night as they aim to keep their momentum going. They face another match on their own patch against Derby County.

It has been revealed that the Rams are in poor form and are in the drop zone along with Burnley and Preston North End. They have won only twice in the league and are five points from safety behind both Lincoln City and Watford after their 2-0 loss at Southampton over the weekend.

Wolves will fancy their chances of securing another win to boost their promotion push as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Stoke City. They are presently sat in 3rd place in the table after 16 fixtures and they are in the play-offs along with Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton, QPR and Swansea City.
